question: What Google Docs-style suggesting behavior is missing or unproved after the main Suggestion package cut, and should Plate restore the old engine or redesign its native review contract?
method: best-api-review/history-v2; redesign-from-first-principles; Best API target and scale gates; Plate/Plite ownership; Chrome live probes; bounded current/main source audits
trigger: User requests harsh honest feedback and a Google Docs behavior audit first, including research in Chrome and experiments in the supplied document, after reporting Enter, cursor, paint and paragraph-boundary regressions.
requirements: Inventory operation-level Google Docs behavior and distinguish live observations, primary-source documentation, historical main behavior, current implementation, and missing proof.

Cover text edits and grouping, paragraph split/merge, soft breaks, marks with prior values, block properties, lists, tables, objects, review, comments, history, persistence, collaboration, native input and scale; do not call a partial browser sample exhaustive parity.

Preserve ordinary feature command capture, accepted-content isolation, contribution identity, retained deleted content, stable positions, dependent author work, atomic decisions and truthful refusals.
Use the supplied Google Doc for synthetic experiments while preserving its original tab; do not send replies, change access, or run destructive bulk decisions across original content.
Compare keep/configure, changed native API, new primitive, hard cuts, owner moves, restoration of main and architecture replacement before choosing one direction.
The latest request is audit-first: persist assessment and recommend one next owner without changing product code or implementing a new API.
evidenceReuse: First suggestions-scope review. Reconsidered related authored research, adoption, scalability and direct-checkpoint records. Reused the recorded performance result only within its frozen workload and did not rerun or refresh that proof. Current producer, consumer, public types, structural tests and browser tests were inspected. Separate bounded read-only workers inspected native/current coverage and main at cce36d378b2f1e5c775dafe1a67c2215165c982c; decisive findings and counts were reconciled locally. Fresh Chrome observations and official sources add behavior evidence. The broad F01-F32 completion interpretation is corrected by a linked current decision, not by modifying immutable history.
summary: Pursue complete suggestion semantics through native per-change details and Plate review. Cut kind-plus-text-ranges as the sole review contract, the first-200-pending card assumption, and silent decision refusals. Keep native authored identity and causal decisions; restoring main would restore duplicate mutation logic and known structural/property limits. Actual Enter/Backspace and valued-mark review lifecycles are the first bounded design question.
alternatives: Keep/configure: existing native contracts and useful tests remain, but current kind/range-only UI cannot express structural identity or exact property changes. More CSS or isolated command patches cannot complete the job.

Change existing API: expose bounded per-change semantic details and structural locations from native authored facts. Plate supplies descriptions, markers, navigation and application policy; the exact public call remains unsettled.

Add primitive: a missing native read capability may earn addition, but a separate Suggestions state store or generic review framework duplicates identity, decisions and Comments lifecycle without a current independent job.

Delete/merge/inline: remove kind/range reduction as the sole review contract, first-page truncation and caller-owned reconstruction of native facts. Keep ranges as useful locations and keep Plate workflow because it has an independent product job.

Move ownership: native content/properties/structure and atomic review belong in Plite; schema normalization belongs to feature commands; wording and interaction belong in Plate; authorization belongs to the application boundary.

Restore main: reject the independent mutation engine as target. Retain and port its useful behavioral expectations, but its paragraph-only split handling and boolean-oriented property rejection do not establish Google Docs parity.

Replace architecture: plain marks, generic before/after diff or mandatory CRDT do not remove required causal identity, retained structure, multi-view and history jobs. No matched evidence justifies replacing the native owner; its runtime representation remains open to later measurement.
proofLimits: 32 families inventoried and reviewed, none excluded. Google evidence: 19 families with a live subset, seven documentation-only, six unresolved; no complete parity certificate. Twenty-five probe rows include repeated actions and selected decisions on a synthetic tab using one author in Chrome/macOS. No second-author Google session, offline replay, real IME, mobile, DOCX roundtrip, full clipboard/move lifecycle or Google benchmark. Current and historical tests were inspected, not rerun. The main manifest counts 19 test files and 101 literal test cases; current WWW has five suggestion tests and Plite authored browser has 39 declarations with parameterization. Model-delta coverage does not imply actual feature-command or UI coverage. No product code, API export, benchmark trial or release changed. Pursue accepts further coupled design work, not a measured new runtime or universal superiority.
